common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating complementary relations from generic similarity. SComGNN (AAAI 2024) models complements as relevant yet dissimilar, combining low-pass and mid-pass graph filters rather than relying solely on similarity smoothing. Revisiting Graph Projections (2025) proposes complementary recommendation through a directed weighted graph projected from user–item interactions—a useful precedent for a lightweight graph branch, although this is not automatically a chronological next-item transition graph. Neither establishes that successive purchases necessarily indicate complementarity. [SComGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130), [Graph Projections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209).

Text can supply additional item signals under sparsity, but published gains may depend on unavailable resources: ITS-Rec (2025) uses pretrained BERT and reviews alongside titles/descriptions, with reviews contributing the largest gains. Its results therefore do not establish the effectiveness of title/description encoders trained from scratch. A benchmark-compatible hypothesis is to augment SASRec with a sparse, training-only directed transition graph, separate source/target embeddings, and a small learned token-pooling encoder over provided titles/descriptions. Keep textual similarity and directional transition scores separate, then learn or validate their mixture. Compare graph-only, text-only, and combined variants using macro validation HR@10 across all four categories; treat compatibility and complementarity as unverified interpretations of observed transitions. [ITS-Rec](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748).

---

Single-negative BCE is a plausible bottleneck, but weak training margins do not establish the cause of Electronics validation performance. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) directly studies SASRec’s negative-sampling overconfidence: increasing negatives and using generalized BCE improves effectiveness; authors recommend 128–256 negatives and correction parameter t=0.75 as practical defaults. This corrects sampling-induced overconfidence, rather than identifying false negatives. [Sampled-softmax research (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) also highlights temperature sensitivity: overly hard negatives can dominate gradients, while in-batch sampling changes popularity pressure without guaranteeing better accuracy.

Recent work supports informative, diverse negatives with safeguards. [Negative Selection and Augmentation (2025)](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/aie2.70004) combines batch/global negative selection with synthetic hard negatives for sequential contrastive learning. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090), broader contrastive-recommendation work, uses a refreshed memory bank and excludes positive/self IDs plus candidates outside a similarity window. These results motivate controlled hardness rather than selecting only the highest-scoring negatives; similarity filtering remains heuristic because unobserved items are not verified dislikes.

Practical experiment proposal: retain SASRec and compare baseline BCE against 128/256-negative gBCE and temperature-tuned sampled softmax. Exclude padding, target duplicates and known training positives; test a modest hard-negative mixture only after uniform sampling. Nonuniform sampled softmax should account for its sampling distribution. Use training histories alone for exclusions, with no future-label access. Select by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and inspect category results; the cited studies do not establish improvement on this benchmark.

---

Recent work supports separate encoders for persistent preferences and recent intent, with learned fusion. TLSTSRec (online 2024) combines temporal information with adaptive long/short-term fusion; hierarchical preference modeling (2025) uses dynamic routing to extract multiple long-term interests, then selects those relevant to recent self-attention features and fuses them using time encoding. These approaches suggest conditioning historical retrieval on current intent rather than pooling all older interactions equally. [TLSTSRec](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051), [hierarchical modeling](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y).

Newer architectures extend this separation across temporal scales. GRELA (2025) introduces gating intended to distinguish local interest from lasting preference shifts. DSRec (September 2026 preprint) pairs a full-sequence Mamba branch with a short-term, time-modulated SSM and residual cross-fusion. TriSSR (2026) motivates separate experts for stable, periodic, and abrupt interest signals, combined through adaptive fusion. These are architectural precedents, not evidence of gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluation. [GRELA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13315), [DSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548), [TriSSR](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925231226009707).

Practical inference for this task: retain SASRec as a causal backbone, add a recent-window intent branch and an attention-pooled historical branch, then learn a gate from their agreement, history length, and observed time gaps. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec encodes interaction histories with item and positional embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward layers. It predicts the next item by scoring candidate embeddings against the sequence representation. Attention selects relevant past interactions, supporting both recent transitions and longer dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
